title: How to Sell Paid Memberships to Your Instagram and TikTok Followers (2026)
html:
Followers are rented. Members are yours. A paid membership turns the people who already watch you every day into a monthly income that does not depend on the algorithm.

The short answer: pick a home for the membership, offer something your free posts do not, set one simple price, then point your Instagram and TikTok bios at it. Instagram and TikTok have their own subscription features, but they ask for a big audience first. On Riftn you can sell a membership from your first follower and keep up to 99% of what fans pay.

Step 1: choose where the membership lives

You have three kinds of home:

  • Inside Instagram or TikTok. Instagram Subscriptions open at about 10,000 followers. TikTok LIVE subscriptions open at about 1,000 followers. Fans pay inside the app, and the platform sets the rules, the fees and the payout dates.
  • A membership site. Tools such as Patreon host the page and take a cut of each payment. You send fans out of Instagram or TikTok to join.
  • A social platform you own a stake in. On Riftn, a membership is a subscription plan on your own profile. Posts, videos and streams can be free, pay-per-view or unlocked for subscribers, and fans can tip any of them.

The deciding questions: how many followers do you need before you can start, how much does the platform keep, and can it close your account and take your members with it?

Step 2: decide what members get

People pay for access, not for more of the same. Strong offers:

  • Early or extended cuts of the videos you already post.
  • Behind the scenes: drafts, outtakes, the making-of.
  • Lessons and templates: the presets, scripts or routines behind your work.
  • Closer contact: members-only live streams, Q&As or a private community.
  • Recognition: a badge, a shout-out, a say in what you make next.

Promise a rhythm you can keep. One members-only post a week beats a daily promise you break in month two.

Step 3: set a price

  • Start with one tier. Three tiers on day one confuse people. Add a higher tier once members ask for more.
  • Price for your niche. Lessons and tools can charge more than fan perks.
  • Make the first month easy. A launch price or a free first week lowers the risk of joining.

Step 4: promote it on Instagram and TikTok

  • Put the link in your bio. It is the main place both apps let you link out. On TikTok, some accounts need more followers before a bio link appears.
  • Show, do not tell. Post a 15-second clip of members-only content with the rest behind the link.
  • Pin a launch post that explains what members get, in one sentence.
  • Mention it at the end of lives, when your most loyal viewers are watching.
  • Thank new members publicly, if they agree. It shows the membership is real.

Keep to each app's rules: link out from your bio and your own posts, and never buy followers or spam comments to promote a paywall.

Step 5: keep members

  • Post on schedule. Members cancel when they forget why they joined.
  • Ask what they want next and make it.
  • Reward long-time members with something the newest ones do not have.

Why creators sell memberships on Riftn

  • No follower minimum. You can sell a membership on your first day.
  • Keep up to 99%. Fans pay you directly through your profile.
  • Paid the moment a fan pays. No payout floor and no monthly wait. See creator payout thresholds compared.
  • Memberships fans can resell. Riftn subscriptions can be tradable, and you earn a royalty when one changes hands. See tokenised subscriptions explained.
  • Fans can pay by card. They do not need crypto to join.

Frequently asked questions

How many followers do I need to sell a membership?

On Instagram, about 10,000 for Subscriptions. On TikTok, about 1,000 for LIVE subscriptions. On Riftn, none.

Can I link to a paid membership from Instagram?

Yes. Put the link in your bio or in a story link sticker. Do not use comments or direct messages to spam the link.

What should I charge for a membership?

Start with one low monthly price that your most loyal fans would pay without thinking, then add a higher tier once members ask for more.

Can I move my members if a platform bans me?

Only if you own the relationship. On a platform that holds your audience, a ban takes the members with it. On Riftn, your followers and your handle, @you@riftn.com, travel with you across the open web.

Riftn is a social media protocol where creators keep the audience and the income. Start your membership on Riftn.
